Selective logging of approximately 50 percent of the merchantable volume is the basic harvest system utilized in treating this type of timber stand. Selective logging on a sanitation - salvage basis with thinning where feasible would improve both the condition and growth of the residual stand on the non-mined areas.
Timber is currently being harvested on Tract III. Westmoreland Resources has indicated that they will make every effort to utilize timber in areas to be mined. If a use cannot be found, there will be no alternative but to bury the downed timber in the pit.
Recreation
The area has a limited recreational value and is used primarily for hunting deer, antelope and game birds.
Within the Sarpy Creek drainage, land forms and vegetative features combine to create good game habitat. Restrictions upon hunting arise at present because the surface lands are in private ownership, with only a few scattered tracts being under Tribal or State jurisdiction. Permission is required for hunting on private lands by Montana law, and owners often post their lands against trespassers.
Use of the Project Area for recreation is limited primarily to the people who live in the area. Much of southeastern Montana is similar to the tracts and there are many developed recreational sites within a day's drive.
